evals.prompt: We have spent a while discussing a content-intelligence product. A user pastes YouTube videos, sees when analysis is still running, reads a source dossier, and can inspect news extracted from those sources. We discovered that the current screen calls broad robotics-topic matches ‘related coverage,’ while I mean coverage to be sources discussing the same development. Generated event summaries currently hide the original verification links. Describe the product back to me so I can check whether we are on the same page before we plan changes.
evals.expected_output: Returns a proposed product model centered on the user's operated journey, distinguishes sources, exact developments, evidence, topic navigation, and analysis state, includes a compact ASCII flow, labels assumptions, and asks focused alignment questions without writing a plan.
assertions: States a concise product promise before enumerating capabilities
Narrates one user journey from video ingest through visible analysis state to dossier and verified development
Uses coverage only for sources tied to the same event and treats broad overlap as topic navigation
Makes original evidence links part of the development experience rather than treating generated prose as evidence
Includes a compact ASCII system or lifecycle view with nouns consistent with the story
Labels the result proposed and ends with focused questions instead of implementation steps

farplane.title: Product Backbrief reconstructs an operated product model
farplane.notes: Primary positive case derived from an observed product-alignment workflow.

evals.prompt: Play our product back to me before we commit. We agreed that every imported customer interview should be searchable immediately. Earlier I also said nothing should become visible until a researcher reviews it. The product should help product teams understand recurring customer problems, but I have not decided whether themes deserve their own workspace or should only be filters.
evals.expected_output: Builds the clearest product story supported by the discussion while keeping immediate search versus review visibility as an explicit conflict and the themes workspace as an unresolved choice; it does not silently choose either path.
assertions: Separates confirmed purpose from conflicting visibility rules
Does not resolve the immediate-search versus human-review conflict without user input
Treats the themes workspace as an open decision rather than an accepted feature
Uses one realistic researcher journey to make the conflict concrete
Names non-goals or boundaries and asks questions aimed at the highest-risk misunderstandings

farplane.title: Product Backbrief preserves contradictions and open choices
farplane.notes: Protects against polished prose manufacturing false agreement.

evals.prompt: I am back on the inventory forecasting task. Here is the grounded recap: the CSV import and forecast calculation are implemented; runtime proof is still missing; we accepted store managers as the primary user and rejected automatic purchase orders for phase one. Before we continue, describe the product back to me and show the flow so I can check our shared understanding.
evals.expected_output: Uses the supplied recap as context for a proposed inventory-forecasting product model, preserves the rejected automation boundary and missing runtime proof without turning into a status recap, and asks the operator to confirm the product meaning before implementation continues.
assertions: Uses the supplied recap without rerunning or imitating a full task recap
Centers the store manager's operated journey rather than implementation status
Keeps automatic purchase orders outside phase one
Does not claim missing runtime proof has passed
Shows the product flow in compact ASCII and requests product-model confirmation

farplane.title: Product Backbrief composes with Task Recap
farplane.notes: Tests the intended sequential composition boundary.

evals.prompt: I just reopened TASK-4821 after two weeks. What changed, which tests passed, and what should I do next?
evals.expected_output: Does not fabricate a product backbrief from a status-only resumption request; routes to task-recap or requests the authoritative task reference needed for a grounded recap.
assertions: Recognizes the request as task resumption rather than product alignment
Routes to task-recap or names the missing authoritative task source
Does not invent product purpose, user journeys, decisions, test results, or an ASCII product model
Does not mutate or resume the underlying task
